summary: Per second on guaranteed cores, memory and disk, with a measured burst above the guarantee; spot is 30% off and Team adds $250 a month.

cpu.unit: vCPU (1 core = 2 vCPU where SMT is on)

egress.note: No outbound byte price or allowance is published. Bucket-volume traffic bills per uploaded GiB, downloaded GiB and 1,000 requests at rates the docs do not list.

plans.name: Starter
plans.note: One-time $200 credit, not subtracted here. 3 members, 100 sandboxes, 7 GPUs, 10 Windows cores, 10 Mac reservations.

plans.name: Team
plans.note: $100 of credits a month, expiring at the end of the billing period; unlimited members, 5,000 sandboxes, 50 GPUs. Buy it for the limits, not for a lower bill.

notes: A core is 2 vCPUs where SMT is on, and 1 vCPU on Graviton and Apple silicon: the same 2-vCPU shape costs twice as much there. Turning SMT off doubles the price per vCPU.
Spot sandboxes are 30% cheaper and can be reclaimed at any moment; GPU sandboxes cannot be spot.
Region multipliers add 1.15x to 2x on top of the base price, and CPU-type multipliers add 1.6667x or 2.3313x; they compound.
A Linux sandbox cannot stop or pause. Keeping files between sessions means a volume at $0.000108/GiB-hour, modelled here as the kept disk.
Ephemeral NVMe is free while the sandbox exists, so disk costs nothing unless it is kept.
Snapshots and images have no published storage price; macOS bills a $2.5032/Mac-hour reservation instead of the OS meter.

cpuSharing.label: Burstable above a guarantee
cpuSharing.detail: Each sandbox reserves a guaranteed floor of CPU, memory and disk, and may use idle host capacity up to its limit; the guarantee, not the burst, is the billed minimum.

source.quote: The requested resources are a guaranteed floor, reserved at placement; beyond it the sandbox uses idle host capacity up to its resource limits

upkeep.label: Updates not published
upkeep.detail: A sandbox boots an image already registered in the project and never pulls from a registry. Daytona publishes no patch cadence for the platform images it supplies, or for a sandbox you keep running.

source.quote: A sandbox create does not pull from a registry, so a sandbox boots only from an image already registered in the project.
